{{Short description|Mathematical theorem of complex manifolds}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Andreotti–Frankel theorem''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|last1=Andreotti|first1=Aldo|author1-link=Aldo Andreotti|last2=Frankel|first2=Theodore|author2-link=Theodore Frankel|year=1959}}, states that if <math> V </math> is a [[smooth algebraic variety|smooth]], complex [[affine variety]] of [[complex dimension]] <math>n</math> or, more generally, if <math>V</math> is any [[Stein manifold]] of dimension <math>n</math>, then 
<math>V</math> admits a [[Morse function]] with critical points of index at most ''n'', and so <math>V</math> is [[homotopy equivalent]] to a [[CW complex]] of [[real dimension]] at most ''n''. 

Consequently, if <math>V \subseteq \C^r</math> is a closed connected complex submanifold of complex dimension <math>n</math>, then <math>V</math> has the homotopy type of a CW complex of real dimension <math>\le n</math>.
Therefore
:<math>H^i(V; \Z)=0,\text{ for }i>n </math>
and
:<math>H_i(V; \Z)=0,\text{ for }i>n. </math>
This theorem applies in particular to any smooth, complex affine variety of dimension <math>n</math>.
